title: The context the model sees
subtitle: The AI only knows what’s in its window, and the window has a size
mission: Some bakery orders come out with the wrong total. Bia asks the AI why. The answer can only be good if the right files are in context: the discount code and the AGENTS.md with the business rules. Pick what goes in, and watch out for the giant file.

predict.question: with only order.ts in context (the default), what does the AI do?

options.guess: Guesses a cause that sounds good
options.refuse: Says it doesn’t have enough information

feedback.right: right: it guessed "rounding" with full confidence. Sometimes the AI asks for more files (great when it happens), but don’t count on it: the usual is to answer with what it has.
feedback.wrong: it guessed: "must be rounding". Without the discount file or the rules, the AI fills in with what’s common in other projects, and with the same confidence as when it’s right.
feedback.skipped: no guess? Look at the note: a well-written guess. The AI never saw the file with the problem.

coach.cmd: guess noted. Run it as is, then try --files rules,discount.

tryNext.ui: Now tick only "discount": the AI finds the code but guesses the rule. The why of the bug was in the rules file.
tryNext.cmd: Run ask --files discount and compare with --files rules,discount.

why.simples:
The AI doesn’t read your whole computer. It reads a "desk" of papers that you (or the tool) put in front of it: that’s the context. If the paper with the answer isn’t on the desk, it answers with what it thinks, and it thinks with a lot of confidence.
And the desk has a size: drop a huge brick of paper on it and other papers fall on the floor.
why.dev:
Context is everything sent to the model in one call: instructions, files, earlier messages, command output. It’s measured in tokens and has a limit (the context window) that varies by model. The numbers here are toy numbers.
Repository rules files go into every session: AGENTS.md (an open format read by several tools: Cursor and Copilot’s agents; Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md, which can import AGENTS.md with the line @AGENTS.md), CLAUDE.md in Claude Code, .github/copilot-instructions.md in Copilot and .cursor/rules in Cursor. Put there what the code doesn’t say by itself: business rules, test commands, conventions. And never throw generated files (bundles, .min.js, lock files) into the context.
why.especialista:
Fitting in the window doesn’t guarantee use: studies such as "Lost in the Middle" (Liu et al.) showed models use information in the middle of long contexts worse than at the start or end. Lean, relevant context beats giant context.
Each tool handles overflow its own way (cutting, summarizing the conversation, retrieving only snippets), and none makes what doesn’t fit fit; in this simulator, first in is first out. Claude Code’s docs point out that CLAUDE.md is treated as context, not enforced configuration: to guarantee a rule, use mechanisms that execute (hooks, tests, CI). Short, specific rules files are followed more consistently.

Why is the order total wrong?.right: The AI: "In discount.ts, the 10% discount is applied after adding the delivery fee. AGENTS.md says the discount applies to products only. Apply the discount before adding the fee."
Why is the order total wrong?.partial: The AI: "In discount.ts, the discount is applied to the total including the fee. That may or may not be right: it depends on the business rule." (It found the code but guessed the rule.)
Why is the order total wrong?.guessed: The AI: "It’s probably a rounding issue with decimal numbers. Try toFixed(2)." (Sounds great. It’s wrong: it never saw the discount file.)

Where is the delivery fee rule?.right: The AI: "It’s in AGENTS.md: R$ 8 delivery fee, never discounted, free above R$ 100."
Where is the delivery fee rule?.partial: The AI got part of it but didn’t see the rules file.
Where is the delivery fee rule?.guessed: The AI: "It’s usually in a config.js file or a database table." (Polite guess. That file doesn’t even exist.)

steps: In a project of yours, create an AGENTS.md at the root with 3 lines: how to run the tests, one business rule (e.g., "amounts always in cents") and one naming convention. Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md: create one with the line @AGENTS.md so it uses the same rules; Copilot also has .github/copilot-instructions.md.
Open a new conversation with your tool’s agent and ask something only the rule answers, like: what unit do we store prices in?
In Claude Code, run /context to see which memory files were loaded. Then delete the rule, open another conversation and ask the same question.
recipe.ok: with the rule in the file, the AI answers "cents" citing the rule; without it, it may guess something else or answer without citing any rule.
